# Flowtr

> Flowtr is a free territory conquest running game for iPhone and Android, made in Lisbon, Portugal. When your run closes a loop, the area inside becomes your territory on a shared world map; other players can take part of it and you can win it back. Not related to Flowtrac or FlowTracer.

Flowtr (em português: «Flowtr — jogo de corrida de conquista de território»; en español: «Flowtr — juego de running de conquista de territorio») is a mobile game for people who run, walk or cycle outdoors and want each activity to count in a competition on the real map of their city.

## Key facts

- Category: territory conquest running game (fitness / health & fitness app).
- Price: free, no ads.
- Platforms: iPhone (App Store) and Android (Google Play).
- How it works: start an activity, close a loop (cross your own trail or return within 25 m of the start), then confirm CLAIM TERRITORY. A loop needs at least 90 seconds in motion and an area of at least 2,500 m². Every claim is validated on Flowtr's server before it appears on the map.
- Rivals: a loop that overlaps another player's territory takes that part (minimum 20 m² and 5% of their area).
- Activity modes: running, walking and cycling share the same map. The mode is detected from average speed; in the global ranking, running counts 100% of the area, walking 60% and cycling 50%.
- Rankings: world, country, city and friends; by week, month or all time; tabs for global score, area, territories and distance.
- Social: follow friends, 1-vs-1 duels and group challenges of up to 50 people.
- Sentinels: virtual rivals created by Flowtr in zones of Lisbon, always labelled as virtual, never presented as real people.
- Where: the map is worldwide; Flowtr was made in Lisbon, Portugal.
- Strava: Flowtr is a game, not an activity log. Runs exported as GPX (e.g. from Strava) can be imported into your personal history but do not claim territory.
- Privacy: other players do not see your full route; shared images and videos hide the first and last 200 m.
